card: This PR hardens Bitcoin Core's read-only BDB parser against crafted wallets that trigger infinite loops, exponential traversal, or out-of-memory exhaustion during wallet migration. It enforces single-visitor traversal for B-tree and overflow pages, limits the aggregate size of page records to the page size, and restricts overflow page payload offsets to valid page bounds. The author demonstrates that an 8 KB crafted file causes master to hang indefinitely, while a 256 KB file inflates memory usage to ~800 MB. The change includes hand-crafted BDB unit tests and updates the BDB fuzz target with expected error strings.
changed_since_previous: No functional changes; the commits and approach remain unchanged from the previous version.
evidence: PR description: 'On master an ~8 KB file built this way doesn't finish.'
PR description: 'A single 64 KB page can turn into ~500 MB this way. On master a 256 KB file took migratewallet from 54 MB to ~800 MB.'
Commit f7e0d7e24b: '34959 added two errors for invalid overflow records, but did not add them to the errors the wallet_bdb_parser target expects, so the target aborts on inputs that reach them.'
problem: Crafted BDB files supplied to `migratewallet` or `bitcoin-wallet` can trigger infinite loops, exponential traversal time, or massive memory inflation. A B-tree page referenced by multiple parent nodes is repeatedly traversed, cycles of empty overflow pages loop indefinitely, and duplicated record index entries or oversized overflow offsets can expand small files into hundreds of megabytes of allocated memory.

risk.why: Flaws in wallet database deserialization could cause valid legacy BDB wallets to fail migration or be falsely rejected as corrupted.

scope_notes: The bulk of the diff (+298 lines) is in unit tests introducing BDBFileBuilder, a test utility that crafts raw binary BDB files byte-by-byte to test parser validation without requiring the Berkeley DB library.
summary: Hardens the read-only Berkeley DB parser used during wallet migration and `bitcoin-wallet` execution against crafted database files. It tracks visited B-tree and overflow pages across tree traversal to prevent duplicate page visits, loops, or shared chains. It also bounds the cumulative size of records on internal and data pages to the page size, and ensures overflow page payload lengths do not exceed page boundaries.
